newsitem.title: UK: LCE cocoa futures in nearby slide as March holds.
newsitem.headline: LCE cocoa futures in nearby slide as March holds.

text.p: Cocoa futures resumed their slide downwards on Thursday in heavy selling after early buying fizzled out and a neutral crop update encouraged long liquidation
Benchmark December prices dropped 14 stg per tonne to a 955 stg close after testing strong resistance, seen by technical analysts at 1,000 stg, with an early 999 stg high.

"There was aggressive selling from trade...people who bought December for fear of a late (Ivory Coast) delivery have been liquidating those positions...there seems to be a reasonable amount of buying for March," said one trader.
"There has been an improvement," said a cocoa analyst commenting on the report by UK crop analysts PCR Ltd. "The prospects have improved. The crop is definitely not going to be late," he added.
Nearby September dropped 14 stg to a close of 955 as overall volume reached a healthy 8,244 lots in late trade.

UK crop analyst PCR gave its latest crop update to private clients on Wednesday but other traders took the view that it more confirmed than altered existing estimates of Ivory Coast's overall March delivery.
PCR is said to have pegged the Ivorian cocoa arrivals at mid-February at around 715,000 tonnes, excluding carry over from the 1995/96 season.

Traders said they understood PCR Ltd sees a marginal improvement, with good pod setting rather than damage after heavy July rains, and an overall output prediction somewhere around 850,000 tonnes, but details were awaited.
"The news has been in the market all day, there weren't many surprises," said another trader.
London selling dominated afternoon trade with New York following.
"London led New York downwards and narrowed the arbitrage gap," said the trader.
Traders pegged resistance at 1,000 stg with a higher level at 1,026 for March for the benchmark second-month December contract.
Richard Gardiner, technincal analyst at Gerald Ltd, expected weakness to continue after December prices scraped key support in mixed Wednesday selling.
"I think it's going to go towards that 965 low," he said this morning
